title: Que cumplás muchos más
desc: A birthday in the patio, and a piece of cake you did not expect
setting: Roberto is thirteen today, the whole street has arrived uninvited, and the pastel is in the middle of the table.

steps.speaker: Roberto
steps.en: Ideay, you came! And what have you got there?

options.es: Felicidades, Roberto. Es una gorra, a ver si te gusta.
options.en: Congratulations, Roberto. It is a cap, let us see if you like it.
options.feedback: Felicidades first and then the present. A gorra is the safest gift there is for a chavalo of thirteen, and it will not come off his head all night.
Fine. The word everybody says as they hand it over is felicidades, and you skipped it.
You came to his birthday with something in your hand. Talking it down on the doorstep is a foreign habit.

steps.speaker: Don Beto
steps.es: Que cumplás muchos más, chavalo. Dígale usted también.
steps.en: May you have many more, lad. You say it to him as well.

options.en: May you have many more, Roberto.
options.feedback: That is the sentence. It is what everybody says at a birthday here, it is the vos form, and nobody will explain it to you twice.
Understood everywhere and it is on the cake. Don Beto handed you the local one and you used the international one.
You said felicidades, which is not the same phrase. Don Beto was teaching you something, not checking up on you.

steps.speaker: Doña Chepa
steps.es: ¡Mírelo! Le empujaron la cara en el pastel. Eso se hace siempre, mijo.
steps.en: Look at him! They pushed his face into the cake. That is always done, love.

options.es: ¿Y eso se lo hacen a todos? Ideay.
options.en: And they do that to everyone? Ideay.
options.feedback: You laughed and asked instead of judging. The answer is yes, to everybody, and Roberto is laughing harder than anyone.

options.en: Oh, I was not expecting that.
options.feedback: Honest and warm. Doña Chepa was inviting you to ask about it.
He is thirteen and delighted. Feeling sorry for him marks the custom as cruel, which is not how anybody in the patio sees it.

steps.speaker: Doña Carmen
steps.es: El primer pedazo para la abuela. Y el segundo para usted, que viene de más lejos.
steps.en: The first piece for the grandmother. And the second for you, who has come the furthest.

options.es: Gracias, doña. Eso no me lo esperaba.
options.en: Thank you, doña. I was not expecting that.
options.feedback: The order of the pieces is the ranking of the room: the oldest, then the visitor who travelled furthest. Being second is being placed.
Enough. Something was just said about where you stand in that patio and it deserved a word.
It sounds generous and it undoes what she just did. She chose the order in front of everybody.
